top_stories.title: Jensen Huang Reinstated as Nvidia CEO After Board Reversal
points: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, reversing its own decision within about 5-11 days after he initially resigned over an affair with a direct report and alleged ties to Chinese intelligence.
Board cited consultations with senior US government officials and concluded reinstatement poses no national security risk; investigation is ongoing, so this is not a final finding.
President Trump publicly and privately lobbied the board for Huang's return, posting that the government sees no risk.

Nvidia stock fell 23% the week before reversal (worst week since October 2008) then jumped roughly 30% on reinstatement news, adding about $1T in market value in a single day—the largest one-day market-value gain in stock market history.

Huang must still testify before Congress: House committee interviews Dec 1-2 and a Senate Banking hearing Dec 3, with Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries calling the saga 'indefensible and incomprehensible.'
Nvidia reported a $115.8B quarterly revenue under interim CFO Colette Kress (up 103% year-over-year), showing business continued functioning normally during the leadership gap.

unique_angles.point: Reversal came specifically Nov 17 (rejection) to Nov 22 (reinstatement), a 5-day span.
Framed as the largest single-day market value jump ($1T) in stock market history.

top_stories.title: OpenAI Launches OpenWorks to Help Small Businesses Adopt AI
points: OpenWorks is a pilot program paying local tech-savvy individuals up to $8,000 per month to work hands-on with small business owners implementing AI.
Runs in 20 U.S. cities, with Rundown AI noting 15 are in the Midwest or South, away from major tech hubs.
Targets independent restaurants, retailers, service firms, and factories; software, venture-backed, and private-equity-owned businesses are excluded.
Participating businesses get 3 free months of ChatGPT Business, and local partners also teach a monthly community AI class, creating a customer pipeline and consulting opportunities.

unique_angles.point: Specifies that 15 of the 20 cities are outside typical tech hubs, in the Midwest or South.

top_stories.title: OpenAI Proposes Industry-Wide Limits on AI Pretraining for Safety
points: OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published pretraining compute scores (a measure of how much computing power went into training a model before fine-tuning) for every major model since GPT-3.5.
Proposal calls for shared industry limits on AI pretraining scale until safety monitoring techniques improve, aiming to create transparency-based shared safety measures across labs.
CEO Sam Altman called it 'the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while.'
OpenAI separately deployed a cheaper GPT-6.2 Sol model as its new default chat model, per The Neuron.

unique_angles.point: Notes OpenAI simultaneously rolled out a cheaper GPT-6.2 Sol as the new default chat model alongside the safety proposal.
Specifies Pachocki published scores for every model since GPT-3.5 and that the ask is for rival labs to agree on shared limits.

items.title: AI Coding Agents Skip Approved Company Code Without Context
points: A DesignVerse study tested two popular coding agents on 15 private codebases (15-20 years old, 1M+ lines of code) across aviation, banking, defense, and other sectors.

Agents used each organization's own approved code in only 55-59% of tasks versus 92% with DesignVerse's own setup; otherwise they invented components or pulled public code despite internal alternatives existing.
Root cause: having access to a codebase isn't the same as knowing which files are the 'blessed' approved ones among a million lines, so agents guess.
Caveat: DesignVerse sells a competing solution and tested its own setup against typical agent configurations, so treat results as a warning rather than an independent benchmark.

items.title: Google's 'My Channel' Patent: Personalized AI Video with Embedded Ads
points: Patent describes an AI system that uses demographic info, watch history, and preferences to generate endless personalized videos starring the viewer as the main character.
Works across genres (crime-comedy, rom-com, sci-fi, action) and can customize context, e.g., placing the viewer in the stands at a cricket match next to their favorite player.
An 'advertising stitcher' weaves sponsor ads directly into the generated video narrative rather than between segments.
Caveat: patents frequently never ship, and Google has not announced launch plans or commented on the filing to 404 Media.

items.title: Meta AI Chief Signals Superintelligence Arrival
points: Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang published an essay declaring 'superintelligence is arriving' and urging the industry to take 'meaningfully different actions' rather than stay on the default path.
Cited Claude's proof of the Riemann hypothesis (a famous unsolved math problem) as evidence AI could soon accelerate research faster than humans can monitor.
Predicted AI models will soon handle all AI research themselves and become 'superhuman' at self-improvement.
Rejected treating superintelligence as inevitable or accepting a 'handover' to AI, diverging from CEO Mark Zuckerberg's typical skepticism toward AI slowdown calls.

items.title: Claude Desktop App Expands Beyond Browser
points: Anthropic released a Claude desktop app for Mac and Windows that syncs chat history with claude.ai accounts.
Mac users can double-tap the Option key from any app to quickly invoke Claude; Windows offers standard installation.
Targets users wanting local access on their own devices, while the browser version remains suited for shared or borrowed computers.

items.title: AI-Powered Market Research Shows Promise
points: Colgate-Palmolive research found large language models using Semantic Similarity Rating (SSR, a technique that numerically scores AI-generated answers) achieved 90% reliability matching real human survey responses.
Technique requires explicit prompting for LLMs to consider demographic attributes when roleplaying (simulating responses as) specific customer types.
Could offer a cost-effective alternative for organizations lacking resources for formal market research, though not a replacement for real human input.

items.title: GLM-5.4: Loop Transformer Efficiency
points: Z.ai's GLM-5.4 uses a 'Loop Transformer' design that cycles through the same layer block multiple times instead of stacking unique layers, cutting total parameters while preserving reasoning depth.
Claims intelligence comparable to models with 2-3 trillion parameters (a trillion = 1,000,000,000,000), rivaling much larger competitors.
Available immediately on the GLM Coding Plan for production coding use.

items.title: Claude Ship: Automated PR Management
points: Three specialized agents handle different pull request stages: Code Review identifies issues, PR Steward applies fixes, and Claude Approvals validates against team policies.
Automates the merging workflow bottleneck, reducing manual review burden on engineering teams.
Part of Anthropic's broader push into agentic systems for enterprise software development.

items.title: Linux Security Without Downtime via Shirudo
points: OpenAI and Cisco's open-source Shirudo creates temporary protective 'shields' that block known exploits in live Linux systems while patches are staged and tested.
Eliminates the need to restart services, maintaining business continuity during security updates.
A collaborative open-source effort aimed at infrastructure security.

items.title: Transformer Architecture Advances
points: Google's DeepCrossAttention (DCA) replaces static residual connections with dynamic routing that selects which prior layers to pass information through, cutting parameters by 30-40%.
Addresses 'information dilution,' where signals degrade through fixed connection paths in traditional transformers.
Testing on large datasets (C4, LM1B) showed faster training convergence and better perplexity (a measure of how well a model predicts text, lower is better) scores than standard architectures.

items.title: Amazon Acquires Decart's AI Optimization Tech for $7.5B
points: Amazon acquired Decart's AI optimization technology for $7.5B to boost efficiency of AI training and inference across hardware platforms.

items.title: Google DeepMind Uses Gemini 4 Agents for Quantum Algorithm Discovery
points: Google DeepMind used Gemini 4 agent teams to discover quantum algorithms 11.8x cheaper for fusion research.
Correctness of the algorithms was verified using the Lean theorem prover (software that formally checks mathematical proofs).
